# Cross-platform Git native proxy projection

metadata:
- checkpoint_id: checkpoint-0aa95e2b70bf
- project_id: codex-git-transport-proxy-projection
- change_type: root-cause
- created_at: 2026-07-26T11:41:25.467351+00:00
- input_signature: 0aa95e2b70bf543510fb183dbeed401f112322b4b0952b21bdb395fe0bb96464

## Summary
GitHub transport failures were caused by projecting the proxy only through HTTP(S)_PROXY across the WSL-to-Windows Git boundary. The network owner now also projects the same approved route through Git native per-process http.proxy configuration without writing user, system, or repository config.

## Changed Files
- workspace/_bridge/codex_network_gateway.py
- workspace/_bridge/codex_environment_mirror_tests.py

## Evidence
- The environment-only Windows Git path repeatedly timed out after about 21 seconds while Git native -c http.proxy on the same remote, credential, and proxy succeeded immediately.
- Work Git and Windows bare Git synchronized at 43afa22a84aff3218676b9f93f8af4c595ae2408.

## Verification
- python3 -m unittest workspace._bridge.codex_environment_mirror_tests: 90/90
- real Windows Git ls-remote through generated transport plan: exit 0
- network/rule/membership/maintainability validators: ok

## Backups
- /home/codexlab/.codex-app/backups/work-git/202607/workflow-governance/20260726-113822-251486-5ee30ae7-local-edit/manifest.json

## Stable Conclusions
- Across WSL-to-Windows Git interop, project an approved proxy route through Git native per-process http.proxy
- environment proxy variables remain compatibility hints, not the sole transport authority.

## Followups
- none recorded

metadata:
